subject: Re: OmniHealth renewal — capacity benchmarking and onboarding concessions
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@omnihealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@omnihealth.com>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@omnihealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and capacity ask — benchmarking questions

Hi Chloe,

We're coming up on our July 2028 renewal and the product team just completed a short bakeoff vs NimbusAI. They flagged two concrete concerns:

- Token latency at 8k context: Nimbus reported 45ms median vs Redwood's 78ms on our sample workloads.
- In pricing simulations, Nimbus' dedicated offering showed ~18% lower projected monthly cost after their quantization recommendations.

Procurement is asking for a performance summary and any possible changes to our renewal terms — specifically: additional onboarding credits, accelerated migration support, and a temporary committed-capacity uplift to cover Q1 usage. They want to decide by 10/14 to align budgets.

Can you share a short, technical summary and what concessions (if any) Redwood can offer to keep OmniHealth on the platform? Happy to set up a call this week.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
VP Product, OmniHealth

Attachment: bakeoff-comparator.pdf (customer-sent)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and capacity ask — benchmarking questions

Hi Sara — thanks for the context and sending the comparator. We take these bakeoffs seriously. Quick plan from our side:

1) Technical baseline: Rishi will run a workload-accurate micro-benchmark against your representative model (same prompt sets / batch sizes) and produce median/95th latency, throughput (tokens/sec), and memory/KV utilization.
2) Cost projection: Neha will produce a 6/12-month committed-capacity uplift proposal plus an optional short-term credit package to offset migration risk.
3) Operational offer: We can propose an expedited onboarding (priority runbook + 24/7 handoff days) if we agree to a short-term uplift commit.

I've attached our internal benchmark plan outline so you know what we'll measure and how. Can you share a small sample of typical requests (anonymized) and available windows to run the baseline? If you prefer a live run, Rishi can join with your infra lead.

I'll coordinate timelines — aiming to get a consolidated response by 10/11 so you have time to take to procurement.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redwood-benchmark-plan.pdf (outline)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed commercial bridge and capacity uplift

Hi Sara — following Chloe's note, attached is a short commercial proposal:

- 3-month committed uplift (x1.5 of your current committed capacity) with a pro-rated price break for the uplift portion.
- $40k onboarding credit to cover migration/testing tasks if you sign the uplift by 10/14.
- 30% professional services discount for the first three months of dedicated onboarding.

If Nimbus is offering migration credits, we are willing to match a portion of that value in exchange for the uplift commitment and a one-year renewal term.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Thurs 10/7 to align on commercial terms. I'll bring a short pricing sheet.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@omnihealth.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Benchmark summary (preliminary) and immediate mitigation steps

Hi Sara — I ran three controlled runs against the sample prompts you shared (batch size 8, sequence 8k, FP16 default). Preliminary numbers vs Omni's sample workload:

- Redwood hosted (g5-like): median latency = 76ms, 95th = 150ms, tokens/sec = 980
- Redwood with compact quant config (INT8-ish path): median latency = 52ms, 95th = 110ms, tokens/sec = 1,420
- Memory profile: KV cache increases memory by ~22% at 8k; enabling our streaming-KV reduces peak memory by ~9% at cost of 3–5ms extra latency per chunk.

Notes / suggestions:
- The 78ms you saw is close to our baseline; we can replicate Nimbus' 45ms with the compact quant path plus a short kernel tuning pass on your model variant. That requires a brief compatibility pass for accuracy (we'll run A/B on a heldout prompt set).
- If you switch to a dedicated pool and apply the compact quant profile, we estimate 15–20% unit cost savings vs your current hosted run and similar end-to-end latency as Nimbus.

Immediate mitigation we can offer:
- 2 weeks of priority kernel tuning for free if we get a short-term uplift commit.
- Dedicated capacity onboarding queue priority (2-week SLA) and a migration playbook.

I'll bake the exact numbers into the deliverable for Chloe/Neha. Happy to present the results to your infra team.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency-report.csv

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@omnihealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@omnihealth.com>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@omnihealth.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal and capacity ask — benchmarking questions

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the numbers — that quant path looks promising. A few points from procurement:

1) Nimbus is willing to provide 3 months of free migration support and a one-time credit equal to ~50% of the onboarding estimate.
2) They also offered a pilot contract to demonstrate parity for up to 6M tokens at no charge.

Those are meaningful incentives. Procurement needs to see either matched commercial value or a stronger operational guarantee (SLA credits / faster onboarding window).

We are open to the 2-week kernel tuning and a short dedicated-capacity pilot if Redwood can commit to:
- A written onboarding timeline (start/end dates) and an SLA credit schedule if milestones slip.
- A one-time onboarding credit equal to $40k+ to match the practical value of Nimbus' package.

I'll share a high-level SOW and procurement timeline (attached). We need a consolidated Redwood position by 10/11.

Sara

Attachment: SOW_draft.pdf

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Escalation: OmniHealth — ask for onboarding credit and priority queue approval

Hi Marissa,

Quick escalation — OmniHealth (strategic account) has a procurement-led decision window to 10/14. They ran a bakeoff and Nimbus is offering migration credits + pilot capacity that create a tangible near-term switching incentive.

What we can offer quickly and what I propose we approve:
- One-time onboarding credit: $40,000 (matches their ask).
- Two-week priority kernel tuning and dedicated-pool onboarding queue (SLA: kickoff within 5 business days of PO).
- 3-month committed uplift at 1.5x current committed capacity with a pro-rated discount on uplift portion; commercial terms handled by Neha.

Rishi's preliminary bench shows parity if we enable the compact quant path + the kernel tuning pass; the remaining risk is time-to-onboard. They asked for an SLA credit schedule if milestones slip — Neha and legal can scope language.

Can you approve the $40k one-time credit and the priority queue commitment so we can get a signed uplift before procurement's 10/14 deadline?

Appreciate the quick review —
Chloe
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
